stem: Bilal places a thin plastic sheet between a bar magnet and a compass needle. On the table he also has a cardboard scrap and a thick steel sheet.

parts.text: What should he expect with the plastic sheet between the magnet and the needle?

options.text: The needle's deflection stays about the same.
The plastic sheet stops the magnetic effect, so the needle no longer deflects.
The cardboard scrap would stop the deflection, but the plastic sheet would not.
The thick steel sheet would also leave the needle's deflection unchanged.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Thin sheets of plastic, cardboard, wood, or glass between a magnet and a compass needle do not stop the magnetic effect, so the deflection stays about the same.

teacher.key_rationale: Plastic, cardboard, and similar non-magnetic sheets do not block the magnet's effect on the needle. Cardboard does not stop deflection either; a thick steel sheet can shield and is not the same case.
